OpenAI did not disclose a technical root cause.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: OpenAI's status record identifies elevated SSO-login errors affecting Login for APIs and ChatGPT. The page displays updates at 08:36 (identified), 09:59 (investigating with gradual recovery), 10:57 (mitigation applied and monitoring), and 15:23 (all impacted services fully recovered) on 16 July 2026; the retrieved page does not state the timezone for those displayed times. The public incident does not disclose a technical root cause.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The governance value of this occurrence is state discrimination: an SSO-path failure should remain distinguishable from account suspension, entitlement loss or broader service unavailability. The evidence establishes the access symptom but not a current VIGIL mechanism such as state collapse, authentication-state propagation failure or verification-dependency failure. The successful invariant is limited to truthful differentiation of the disclosed SSO service-failure state. The cause remains an unresolved material question, preventing a whole-occurrence invariant-held conclusion. SSO outage is not established as a governance-baseline integrity failure or planned GAI deactivation, and application of SDOS or the selected NIST Profile action remains unresolved. No external requirement finding or broader authentication-architecture conclusion is supported. Independent occurrence-level external assessment finds affirmative, source-bounded repair in the reported restoration stage. Relevant communication/incident-process requirements remain Boundary where the decisive plan or implementation record is not public. Requirements addressing a different technical object, lifecycle or source date remain audit-only; voluntary adoption is not a gate.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: This incident shows why observability should report the affected access layer precisely even when the underlying root cause is unknown. Clear state labelling helps users avoid interpreting authentication-path failure as an account or policy decision.
